<description>
`sign_ecdsa(..., rfc6979=True)` in the test framework derives the nonce from the raw message hash. RFC6979 section 2.3.4 (bits2octets) reduces the hash mod n first. libsecp256k1 has done so since 0.2.0. So for a hash >= n the framework's signature differs from libsecp256k1's, though it is still valid.

This is a small, correct fix with a test. The test checks two signatures computed with libsecp256k1, one of them for a hash >= n, and fails without the fix. The change has no practical effect on current tests: the only caller, `feature_taproot.py`, signs double-SHA256 sighashes, which are >= n with probability about 2^-128. If reviewers see no benefit, feel free to close it.
</description>

<commits>
bb96838c9d test: reduce hash mod n for RFC6979 nonce

RFC6979 section 2.3.4 (bits2octets) reduces the message hash modulo the
group order before it enters the nonce derivation. libsecp256k1 has
done so since 0.2.0. The test framework used the raw hash, so for a
hash >= n its deterministic signature differed from libsecp256k1's.

Add a test with signatures computed by libsecp256k1, one of them for a
hash >= n.
</commits>
